fields: What should an architect define before selecting Claude architecture components?
The measurable business outcome, constraints, and success criteria.
Why is “we need an AI agent” not a complete requirement?
It names an implementation preference rather than the underlying outcome and constraints.
Which requirements should remain deterministic when correctness must not depend on probabilistic output?
Hard rules such as authorization, numeric thresholds, and schema validation.
Why is a production Claude system more than a model call?
Because the request path also includes identity, context, tools, state, verification, outputs, observability, and recovery.
What should be designed alongside the happy path?
The failure and recovery path.
What should remain authoritative for current transactional facts?
The system of record, not chat history, a vector index, or a cached summary.
What distinguishes a workflow from an agent in Anthropic's architecture guidance?
A workflow follows predefined code paths; an agent dynamically decides how to accomplish the task and use tools.
When is a workflow generally preferable to an agent?
When the process can be enumerated in advance and benefits from predictability and control.
When is an agent justified?
When required steps cannot be reliably predetermined and dynamic planning/tool use provides measured benefit.
What is the orchestrator-worker pattern?
A lead agent decomposes work, delegates bounded subtasks, and synthesizes worker results.
What are strong reasons to use multiple agents?
Context isolation, parallel independent work, and meaningful specialization.
What is prompt chaining?
A sequence where each stage consumes the previous stage's output.
What is routing?
Classifying an input and sending it to the appropriate specialized path.
Why is model-token cost alone insufficient for architecture comparison?
Total solution cost also includes engineering, infrastructure, human review, monitoring, incidents, and compliance overhead.
What must exist before claiming a business improvement?
A baseline and measurable outcome.
Outcome requirement
The measurable value or change the solution should create.
Risk constraint
A condition defining what the system must not do without stronger controls.
System of record
The authoritative source for current operational state.
Idempotent retry
A retry that can safely repeat without duplicating an unintended side effect.
Workflow
LLM/tool orchestration through predefined code paths.
Agent
A system where the model dynamically directs its own process and tool use.
Orchestrator
The component that interprets the goal, decomposes work, delegates, and synthesizes results.
Context isolation
Keeping independent worker contexts separate to reduce interference and pollution.
Parallelization
Run independent subtasks concurrently and combine their results.
Routing
Classify an input and send it to the appropriate specialized path.
Technical metric
A system measure such as task success, latency, throughput, token use, or cost per task.
Business metric
An outcome such as time saved, cases resolved, error reduction, revenue impact, or customer satisfaction.
Architecture should begin with the {{c1::business outcome}}, not the preferred AI component.
Hard authorization rules belong in {{c1::deterministic controls}} rather than relying only on prompts.
Convert vague goals into {{c1::measurable targets}} before choosing a model or pattern.
For stateful workflows, define {{c1::state ownership}} explicitly rather than treating model context as durable state.
Design the {{c1::failure path}} at the same time as the happy path.
Current transactional facts should come from the {{c1::system of record}}.
A {{c1::workflow}} follows predefined paths, while an agent dynamically chooses its process.
Prefer the {{c1::least autonomous}} pattern that still meets the requirement.
Multi-agent systems are justified by meaningful {{c1::isolation, parallelism, or specialization}}, not by novelty.
The orchestrator should verify {{c1::coverage and worker outputs}} before synthesis.
Use {{c1::parallelization}} only when subtasks are genuinely independent.
An {{c1::evaluator-optimizer}} loop needs measurable evaluation criteria, not vague critique.
Before claiming improvement, define a measurable {{c1::baseline}}.
Compare architectures using {{c1::total solution cost}}, not model-token cost alone.

What should drive Claude model selection?
Measured workload requirements across quality, latency, cost, tool use, context needs, and risk.
Why should model names not be hard-coded as permanent architecture assumptions?
Model lineups have lifecycle states and change over time.
What should happen after changing the model in production?
Re-run workload-specific regression, latency, safety, and cost evaluations.
What is the role of a system prompt in architecture?
To provide trusted behavioral instructions, scope, constraints, and output expectations.
Why is a system prompt not an authorization boundary?
Model compliance is probabilistic; protected actions need enforceable controls outside the model.
How should untrusted retrieved/user content be handled relative to trusted instructions?
Keep it structurally separated and do not allow it to silently redefine policy.
When should few-shot examples be added?
When representative examples measurably improve ambiguous behavior, formatting, tone, or boundary cases.
What is zero-shot prompting?
Giving clear task instructions without examples.
What is the key principle of context engineering?
Put the smallest useful set of high-signal information in the model's active context for the current decision.
Why is more context not automatically better?
Irrelevant or stale context consumes tokens and can compete with relevant information.
What content is a strong candidate for prompt reuse/caching?
Large stable instructions or reference material reused across many requests.
What content is a poor caching candidate?
Frequently changing transactional state that must be current.
Active model
A fully supported model recommended for current use.
Deprecated model
A model still functional for a period but no longer recommended and scheduled for retirement.
Behavioral instruction
Prompt guidance that influences how the model should act.
Enforceable control
Code, permissions, schema, policy, or approval logic that guarantees a boundary outside model compliance.
Zero-shot
Clear direct instructions without worked examples.
Few-shot / multishot
Representative examples included to demonstrate desired behavior.
Active context
Information currently visible to the model for the present inference.
Compaction
Compressing a long interaction into a smaller representation that preserves important state and decisions.
Prompt template
Reusable stable prompt structure with request-specific variables.
Choose the model that meets the workload's {{c1::quality threshold}} at acceptable latency and cost.
Model migration should be treated as a {{c1::production change}} and re-evaluated.
Use prompts to guide behavior; use {{c1::deterministic controls}} to enforce hard security and policy invariants.
Keep trusted instructions structurally separate from {{c1::untrusted user or retrieved content}}.
If a clear zero-shot prompt already passes the eval, extra examples may add {{c1::unnecessary tokens and maintenance}}.
Prompt engineering should respond to {{c1::observed evaluation failures}}, not ritual complexity.
The context window should be treated as a finite {{c1::working set}}, not a database.
Large corpora are often better handled with {{c1::just-in-time retrieval}} than by preloading everything.
Reuse is safest when the content is {{c1::stable enough}} that freshness is not compromised.
Agent Skills use {{c1::progressive disclosure}} so detailed resources can load only when relevant.

Why can exposing more tools to an agent be harmful?
It expands potential blast radius and can also make tool selection harder.
What is the least-privilege goal for agent tools?
Expose only the capabilities, data, credentials, and side effects required for the task.
When can broad shell or filesystem tools be appropriate?
When the use case truly needs general-purpose capability and the environment, credentials, and permissions are strongly constrained.
What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
Authentication establishes identity; authorization determines what that identity may do.
Why is a user message saying “I am an administrator” not authentication?
Identity must come from a trusted authentication mechanism, not untrusted prompt text.
Why can adding a reranker or extra tool/model stage hurt a system even if quality improves?
Each extra stage adds latency and often cost, so the gain must justify the operational impact.
What work should be parallelized to reduce wall-clock latency?
Truly independent operations with no hidden dependency.
Why is logging only the final model answer insufficient for agent debugging?
Failures can occur in retrieval, tool calls, orchestration, or external state before the final answer.
What does an agent trajectory capture?
The sequence of model decisions, tool calls, and intermediate interactions during a run.
What is the core purpose of RAG?
Retrieve relevant external knowledge and place it in model context at inference time.
Why does chunking matter in RAG?
Poor chunk boundaries can split semantic units and reduce retrieval relevance or interpretability.
